en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Tenth Chapter
The Discourse on Effort:
Are the five types of sensory consciousness accompanied by effort?
Yes, they are.
Is it not the case that the five types of sensory consciousness have arisen bases and arisen objects?
Yes, they do.
If the five types of sensory consciousness have arisen bases and arisen objects, then indeed, you should not say: [that they are dissociated from the mind].
“The five types of consciousness are with effort.
Is it not the case that the five types of consciousness have bases that have arisen prior to them, objects that have arisen prior to them, internal bases and external objects,
unmixed bases and unmixed objects, diverse bases and diverse objects, and do not share one another’s domain or sphere?

They experience [them]; they do not arise without attention, they do not arise without mental engagement, they do not arise without succession, and they do not arise neither before nor after one another—is it not the case that the five types of sensory consciousness do not arise as immediate antecedents for one another?
Yes, it is so.
If the five consciousnesses do not arise as immediate antecedents for one another, then surely it should not be said that "the five consciousnesses are with effort.
Is eye-consciousness with effort?
“Yes.
“Then you must say that eye-consciousness arises having emptiness as its object?
“Certainly not,” you reply. … [and so on] …
Is eye-consciousness that arises having emptiness as its object? Yes.
Does eye-consciousness arise in dependence upon both the eye and emptiness?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it the case that visual consciousness arises in dependence upon both the eye and emptiness? Yes.
“Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and emptiness”—is there such a sutta?
No, there is not... [as before]...
“Visual consciousness arises dependent on the eye and forms”—
is this indeed a sutta? Yes.
If it is true that “dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises”—
as this sutta passage indeed exists— then surely, sir, you should not say:
“Dependent on the eye and emptiness, eye-consciousness arises.”
Is eye-consciousness accompanied by mental effort? Yes.
Does eye-consciousness arise by taking as its object that which is past or future? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is eye-consciousness accompanied by effort? Yes.
Does eye-consciousness arise by taking contact as its object …pe… by taking tangible objects as its object?
Certainly not; it should not be so stated …pe…
Is mental consciousness accompanied by effort, and does mental consciousness arise having emptiness as its object? Yes.
Is visual consciousness accompanied by effort, and does visual consciousness arise having emptiness as its object?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Mental consciousness is accompanied by mental effort;
does mental consciousness arise by taking the past and the future as its object? Yes.
Eye-consciousness is accompanied by mental effort; does eye-consciousness arise by taking the past and future as its object?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...mental consciousness is accompanied by mental effort; does mental consciousness [arise] by taking contact as its object... [and so on]?
Does it arise with contact as its object?
Yes. Does eye-consciousness involve mental effort? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise with contact as its object? ... [and so on] ... Yes.
“Does it arise with the tangible as its object?
One should not say so… [and so on]… It should not be said—
“Are the five types of consciousness accompanied by mental effort?”— Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:

“Here, monks, having seen a form with the eye, a monk grasps at its signs … [as before] … he does not grasp at its signs … [as before] … having touched a tactile object with the body, he grasps at its signs … [as before] …”
“He does not grasp at signs.
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
In that case, the fivefold consciousness is with effort... [etc.
...The discussion on "with effort" is finished.
